# earshot

**Ears for coding agents.**

<!-- launch video -->
[**Watch the 22 s launch film**](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/earshot/releases/tag/v0.1.0) - every sound in it was made
in code by `earshot forge`; no recordings, no music track.

![Frames from the launch film](docs/media/launch_frames.png)

AI coding agents can now write the code that renders a film, a product demo or a game. They still cannot hear what
they made. They cannot tell a premium key press from a cheap one, notice that a hit lands 80 ms after the cut, or
hear that the music swells in the wrong place.

earshot turns sound into evidence an agent can reason about: what a file sounds like in words, how well it fits a
description, the best moment inside a long recording, whether it is a real recording or code-synthesized, a
second-by-second listening transcript of a whole film, an annotated picture of it, and a scorecard against
professional launch films. It runs locally on CPU, as a CLI, a Python API and an MCP server.

With ears, an agent can also **make its own sounds in code** and improve them by listening (`earshot forge`), and
**translate a recording into code** it can vary (`earshot fit`). Both below.

**New in 0.3: sound for code-made films.** A bank of 201 sound effects stored as code that render by id in seconds,
with no models and no network: `earshot sfx` aims a whoosh, hit, click or note at a moment in the picture, and
`earshot kit` renders a whole film's effects with measured sync points ([below](#sound-for-films-bank-sfx-kits)).

```
$ earshot describe enter.ogg
  0.56 s short transient (attack 3 ms, decays in 190 ms). Sounds most like: a single mechanical keyboard key press
  (z +5.4), a soft key release click (z +3.6) ... [clear reading]. peak -0.1 dBFS, brightness 1.5 kHz ...

$ earshot match key.ogg "a deep thocky mechanical keyboard press" --alts "a clicky blue switch keyboard" "a mouse click"
  -> strong (z +3.7; would rank #2 among 322 vocabulary descriptions) ...

$ earshot find keys.ogg "a single mechanical key press" --top 4
  0:03.94-0:04.19 (0.24 s stroke, z +4.1 strong); 0:10.60-0:10.86 ...

$ earshot critique film.mp4
  VERDICT: close - 21 of 23 scored metrics in range ... FIX FIRST: 1. [major] nothing reaches body level until 0:01.01 ...
```

## What it does

| command | what an agent gets |
|---|---|
| `describe FILE` | what it sounds like: calibrated tags (z) with the closest alternative readings, AudioSet labels, measurements |
| `match FILE QUERY [--alts ...]` | how well a description fits: cosine, z among the vocabulary, a verdict (strong / plausible / weak / no match) with held-out evidence |
| `rank QUERY PATHS...` | many candidate files sorted by a description (pick the best download) |
| `find FILE QUERY` | the best moments inside a long recording, as sample trims (start / end seconds) |
| `compare FILE --refs DIR` / `ab A B` | nearest reference recordings and typicality; A/B two sounds or two trims, the differences in words |
| `realness FILE...` | real recording / pro-produced vs code-synthesized, with evidence and per-window scores |
| `timeline FILE [--video V] [--cues C]` | the listening transcript: events (time, level, tag), sections, loudness, beat grid, sync of sound to picture cuts and cue frames |
| `sheet FILE -o out.png` | an annotated PNG (video frames, sections, labelled events, spectrogram, waveform, loudness, sync markers) for agents that read images |
| `critique FILE [--video V]` | a launch-video scorecard against a profile of 7 professional launch films, with timestamped fixes |
| `profile REFS... -o p.json` | build your own reference profile from films you admire |
| `measure FILE` | objective measurements only (no models): LUFS, true peak, LRA, envelope, spectrum, tempo / key |
| `forge RECIPE --refset CAT` | make a sound in code and improve it by listening (see below) |
| `fit FILE -o recipe.py` | translate a recording into a forge recipe module that re-renders it, with knobs and morphs (see below) |
| `sfx render ID -o x.wav` | a sound from the shipped bank of 201, aimed at the picture (`--dur`, `--apex`, `--pitch`) and audited; `sfx list`, `sfx check` (no models) |
| `kit init / render / check` | a film's sound kit: one bank sound per role, rendered into cached takes with measured onset / peak / end (no models) |
| `gallery DIR -o page.html` | one static HTML listening page of forge outputs: players, spectrograms, numbers |
| `llm FILE --yes-upload` | optional audio-LLM critique (Gemini), only with your own key and explicit consent |
| `mcp` | the same tools as an MCP server for Claude Code and other agents |
| `doctor [--load]` | check the install, models, data files and CPU settings |

Every command prints a plain-language summary first; `--json` gives the full result, `--out f.json` saves it. Errors
are one line on stderr (`earshot <command>: error: ...`, exit 1). Each CLI call is a new process and loads the models
(~20-40 s) before it answers (`measure`, `sfx` and `kit` load none): for more than a few calls use the MCP server
(models stay loaded) or one Python script with `from earshot import api`.

What an agent sees when it listens to that film with `earshot sheet` (frames, labelled sound events, spectrogram,
loudness, sync to the beat):

![earshot sheet of the launch film](docs/media/launch_sheet.png)

## Make sounds: earshot forge

Listening makes iteration possible. The agent writes a sound as code: a **recipe** of physical synthesis (modal
resonators, contact excitations, filtered noise, a computed room and a microphone; no recorded audio inside). The
forge renders candidates from the recipe's parameters, and a **critic** built from earshot scores each one:
description match against named confusions, realness, closeness to real reference recordings and measured shape, then
model-free penalties against the references: 1/3-octave tonal balance, the spectro-temporal envelope (a tail that dies
too fast shows here), artifacts (clicks, aliasing, DC / infrasound, harsh resonances, comb ring, cut tails, clipping)
and polish (attack, onset snap, tail smoothness). A cheap model-free **pre-screen** ranks many renders with the same
measurements, so the models only hear the best; an evolutionary **search** keeps the best and mutates them. Then the
agent reads the critic's words ("sounds like: a cork pop, a glass ting", "decay +2.4 outside the refs", "bumpy tail"),
looks at spectrograms next to the references, rewrites the recipe, and runs it again.

```bash
earshot forge --list                             # the recipes (click, impact, keypress, pop, whoosh, ...) + refsets
earshot forge keypress --refs path/to/real/keypresses/ --budget 144 --variants 4 --dir made/keypress
earshot forge whoosh --refset whoosh_fast --budget 96 --dir made/whoosh      # a reference set's 'forge' split
earshot forge whoosh --target "a fast crisp air whoosh" --alts "a wind gust" "a sword swing" \
  --refs path/to/real/whooshes/ --mode real --dir made/whoosh
earshot forge --render keypress --params made/keypress/report.json --seeds 1 2 3 --dir made/again
```

Output (`--dir`): the best diverse sounds as WAVs; `report.md` (what was asked, the search per generation, each pick in
the critic's words, the measured gap to the references); `compare.png` (each pick's spectrogram, envelope and
1/3-octave balance next to its nearest reference); `audition.wav` (made, ref, made, ref ... to listen in pairs);
`report.json` with every candidate's parameters and scores, the same critic's scores of the real references
(leave-one-out) and held-out AudioSet tags. Picks are re-rendered on new seeds (`--robust`, default 3) and must differ
in parameters and in sound. Reference sets (`earshot/forge/refsets.py`) are split by source into a 'forge' side the
search may use and a 'bench' side only the fixed benchmark (`eval/forge/bench.py`) hears. The DSP toolkit for recipes:
`earshot/forge/dsp.py` (sources: modal, noise, air, sweeps, Shepard risers, sub drops, bells, FM; layering) and
`earshot/forge/fx.py` (reverb, saturation, transient shaping, limiter, EQ match, Doppler, filters, glitch, granular).
In Python: `from earshot.forge import forge`.

**forge v2 (0.2.0).** Recipes come as families of named characters: 34 motion-design categories (whooshes, swishes,
swipes, risers, downlifters, zips, impacts, sub drops, logo stings, clicks, taps, toggles, hover ticks, pops,
notification dings, shimmers, glitches, key presses), 16 of them modelled on the designed effects of professional
launch films ([docs/motion-sfx-study.md](docs/motion-sfx-study.md)), 4-6 variants each. A fixed benchmark scores them
against held-out recordings the forge never heard. Against v1 on it: variants are no longer near copies (CLAP cosine
between variants 0.89-0.97 -> 0.71-0.85 in the five categories v1 had; real sets 0.52-0.77), tails that died too fast
now reach the real length (click t40 0.56 -> 1.44 x the bench median, fast whoosh 0.51 -> 0.88), and the tonal
balance is closer in 3 of those 5 (key press 8.2 -> 7.4 dB, fast whoosh 8.6 -> 6.2, impact 6.7 -> 4.4). Across all
34, the made balance is at least as close to the held-out recordings as a second set of real recordings in 18 of the
21 categories that have a number, and every final re-renders from its `report.json` (`earshot forge --check`). The
model checks that v1 had saturated fell. A clean blind-test kit for the v2 sounds is `eval/forge/blind_v2.py`; no v2
score is published yet (docs/SFX.md says the same), so the blind test below is the v1 one. What changed, every number, and what is still weak: [docs/FORGE_V2.md](docs/FORGE_V2.md).

The reference recordings are licensed and not in this repo, so `--refset` needs a local registry: bring your own refs
with `--refs DIR`, or lay them out as described in `earshot/forge/refsets.py`. Without refs the critic runs in
designed mode (realness reported, not required). The CLI defaults changed in 0.2.0 (pre-screen, seed bank, robust
re-renders, the recipe's reference set); the Python `forge()` defaults still reproduce v1. See
[CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

**Blind test (v1 recipes).** A key press, a UI click, a pop, a fast whoosh and an impact were made from scratch in
code and played blind next to real recordings of the same kind of sound. The author picked the made one correctly **8 times out
of 15**: a coin flip. Only the made impact was spotted (its tail dies too fast). One listener and 15 trials is a small
test, not a proof; it says the made sounds are no longer easy to tell from real ones.

**Honest limits (Goodhart).** The search optimises earshot's own models, and those can be pleased without the sound
getting better. After a search the made sounds pass every model check, held-out ones included, so the model checks
stop telling made from real; the 1/3-octave measurement still can. The realness model is easy to fool (a modal
resonator plus a room and a noise floor reads "real"). Judge a made sound by the model-free measurements,
spectrograms next to the references, robust re-renders, and a human blind test.

## earshot fit: audio to code

`earshot fit` translates a recording into code by analysis by synthesis. It fits a small synthesis model with readable
parameters (ringing modes, tracked partials, a time-varying noise gesture, or a layered hybrid of them) until its
render matches the recording, then writes the model as a forge recipe module whose `render()` makes the sound. The
module stores the structure of the sound, not its samples, so it can make new takes, variations (size, damping,
pitch, brightness, decay, ...) and morphs between two recordings.

```bash
earshot fit click.wav -o made/click_fit.py --report    # recipe + its render + side-by-side spectrogram + metrics
python made/click_fit.py 3 take3.wav                   # the module renders on its own (seed 3)
earshot fit --morph a.wav b.wav --amount 0.5 -o made/ab_morph.py
earshot fit --forge made/click_fit.py --budget 96 --dir made/click_variations   # critic-searched variations
```

Measured on 12 real recordings (2 each of click, key press, pop, impact, fast whoosh, notification): median CLAP
cosine 0.945 between each recording and the render of its generated code (minimum 0.881), and the same top
`earshot describe` tag in 10 of 12. In our 12-trial blind test (recording vs render, loudness-matched, random order)
the listener could not tell which clip was the recording. One listener is a small test, not a proof. The renders are
close, not identical: onsets, tone balance and noise texture still differ measurably; the selection weights were set
on the same 12 recordings; risers, zips and long designed sounds are untested. A fit is a derivative of its recording,
so keep the source's licence with the recipe. Limits: [docs/FIT.md](docs/FIT.md#limits-honest).

## Sound for films: bank, sfx, kits

The forge's delivered sounds ship as a bank that renders by id, with no models and no network: 183 forge v2 finals
(34 categories), each stored as its render block and re-rendering its delivered WAV to one 24-bit step, three tuned
kalimba voices, and 15 sounds fitted from CC0 recordings (clicks, a tick, pops, touches, keys, a snap, a bell, a
whoosh; credits in [docs/CREDITS_FIT.md](docs/CREDITS_FIT.md)). A film pipeline renders from it in seconds; searching
and fitting new sounds stay offline steps.

```bash
earshot sfx list --kind whoosh                                      # ids, lengths, peak times, cue kinds, knobs
earshot sfx render whoosh_fast/crisp -o w.wav --dur 0.8 --apex 0.32  # a new take aimed at a move (--seed N)
earshot sfx render pluck/kalimba -o e5.wav --pitch E5                # tuned through the recipe's own f0
earshot sfx check w.wav                                              # clicks, cut tails, clipping, ring, rising glides
earshot kit init --preset calm -o audio/kit.json                     # calm | crisp | minimal
earshot kit render audio/kit.json --out audio/kit                    # takes + kit.lock.json (measured onset / peak / end)
```

- **Knobs** edit each recipe's own parameters, never resample: `dur` lands exactly, `apex` puts a whoosh's loudest
  moment within 5 ms of the target (measured within 2.5 ms), `pitch` takes a note name or Hz (pluck E5, a bell G5, a
  sub drop G1 measure 0 cents off); noise sounds refuse a pitch and say why.
- **The audit** (`earshot sfx check`, run on every render) is measurement only: clicks, cut tails, clipping, DC, comb
  ring, a re-rising tail, a tonal pitch that climbs more than 4 semitones (the rising "synth whip"), and for hits,
  stacked attacks or a build before the hit. 185 of the 201 sounds are clean; the presets use none of the others.
- **Kits** name one sound per role (tick, hit, whoosh.short, key, bell, text ...). `kit render` writes deterministic,
  cached takes and a lock with each take's measured sync points; a take that fails the audit is re-rolled on a new
  seed. The three presets sound every role but riser, swell and suck, use one clean hit for the lockup, and use the
  fitted recordings for clicks, ticks, keys, touches and the snap where they measure closer to the role than the
  forge member (earshot match and realness).
- **Python and MCP**: `from earshot.forge import bank; y, meta = bank.render('pro_sub_drop/ref', pitch='G1')`;
  `earshot.api.sfx_render / kit_render`; MCP tools `sfx_list`, `sfx_render`, `kit_render`.

Full reference (every knob, the audit, the kit and lock formats, the presets role by role, fit entries from
public-domain recordings, measured cost): [docs/SFX.md](docs/SFX.md). How cinetic uses it:
[docs/INTEGRATION.md](docs/INTEGRATION.md#cinetic-uses-earshot).

## Gallery

`earshot gallery` turns forge outputs into one static HTML page for people with ears: no server, no network, no
external scripts, inline CSS. One card per category, grouped by family (whooshes, sweeps, impacts, UI, tonal,
digital); per sound a player, a spectrogram thumbnail (log frequency, one time span per card so lengths compare),
duration, peak and momentary-max LUFS, the critic's total / pass, and the recipe parameters of every variant in a
collapsible table. The repo holds no audio, so point it at your own forge runs (`out/forge_v2` below is one folder
per category).

```bash
earshot gallery out/forge_v2 -o out/gallery/gallery.html                  # <category>/final/*.wav (+ report.json)
earshot gallery out/forge_v2 -o g.html --results eval/forge/results_v2r6.json   # + held-out benchmark numbers
earshot gallery out/forge_v2 -o g.html --refs forge                        # + A/B row: each sound's nearest forge ref
earshot gallery --compare "r2:out/forge_v2/*/final_r2" "r3:out/forge_v2/*/final" -o compare.html \
  --results r2:eval/forge/results_v2r2.json                                # before / after, variant under variant
earshot gallery out/forge_v2 -o portable.html --embed                      # audio (FLAC) + images inside the file
earshot gallery out/forge_v2 -o share.html --embed-compressed              # one small file: MP3 previews, plays anywhere
earshot gallery --compare "v1:old/*/final" "v2:out/forge_v2/*/final" --alias keypress=typing_key -o v1_v2.html
```

Audio is referenced by relative path (or embedded with `--embed`); thumbnails go to `<page>_files/` next to the page
and are cached by content. `--embed-compressed` makes one self-contained page to send or open on a phone: each sound
encoded by ffmpeg (MP3 192 kbps by default; `--embed-codec opus` or `vorbis` for Ogg, `--kbps` for the rate), JPEG
thumbnails, no links to local files; 183 sounds come to about 9 MB. The numbers on it are still measured on the WAVs.
`--alias OLD=NEW` puts a folder under another category's card (an older recipe's `keypress` under `typing_key`).
A "match loudness" switch (on by default) turns louder players down so a riser does not blast after a click; it
changes the player volume only, never the files. Benchmark numbers are shown only for files the benchmark actually
measured: a file newer than the results JSON, or with another length / peak, gets none (renamed files are matched by
length and peak, and the page lists every such case). In `--compare`, files identical to an earlier version are marked
`= r2`. Bench references never go on a page: `--refs bench` is refused, every reference passes `refsets.held_out()`,
and only the benchmark's numbers are shown, never its file names. Forge references are licensed recordings: keep a
page that plays them private. In Python: `from earshot.gallery import gallery`.

## Install

Python 3.10+ and ffmpeg / ffprobe on PATH. CPU only; no GPU is used.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Leonxlnx/earshot && cd earshot
python -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu   # Windows: .venv/Scripts/python
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -e ".[mcp,llm,dev]"
.venv/bin/python -m earshot doctor --load
```

The first model use downloads two open models (~1.1 GB) into `.cache/hf` inside the repo (or `EARSHOT_HOME`), each at
a pinned revision with safetensors weights: CLAP `laion/larger_clap_general` @ `16c8cc3` (text-audio embeddings; the
Hub's safetensors conversion of its main revision) and the AudioSet tagger `MIT/ast-finetuned-audioset-10-10-0.4593`
@ `f826b80`. `earshot doctor --fetch` downloads them up front. After that earshot loads them from that cache only and
never contacts the Hub; a damaged cache is an error that names the folder, not a silent new download.

Offline: `EARSHOT_OFFLINE=1`, `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` and `TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1` all mean the same to earshot: it never
downloads, and a model missing from the cache is an error that says so. earshot never sets or clears these variables.

A cache made before 0.2.1 holds CLAP's main revision `ada0c23`, whose only weights are a pickle (`pytorch_model.bin`,
the same tensors). earshot still loads it from the cache (torch `weights_only`), never downloads it, and `earshot
doctor` says so; `earshot doctor --fetch` downloads the pinned safetensors (776 MB), used from then on.

Settings (environment variables): `EARSHOT_THREADS` (torch CPU threads, default min(4, cores/2)), `EARSHOT_HOME`
(cache root), `EARSHOT_PRECISION` (`bf16` by default, used only on CPUs with native bf16 such as AVX512-BF16 / AMX,
fp32 everywhere else; `fp32` forces fp32), `EARSHOT_OFFLINE=1` (above), `EARSHOT_CLAP` / `EARSHOT_AST` (another
Hub model id, or a local model folder with `config.json` and `model.safetensors`, which loads from disk as it is with
no network and is never downloaded into) and `EARSHOT_CLAP_REVISION` / `EARSHOT_AST_REVISION` (another Hub revision;
safetensors weights only). A custom Hub model downloads its top-level config, tokenizer and safetensors files by name,
never a repo's subfolders or weight variants.
`earshot doctor` reports the revisions and what the cache holds; `--load` also what loads (revision, weights,
precision).

### MCP server for Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add earshot --scope user -e EARSHOT_THREADS=3 -- /path/to/earshot/.venv/bin/python -m earshot mcp
```

Or in any client's `.mcp.json`:

```json
{"mcpServers": {"earshot": {"command": "/path/to/earshot/.venv/bin/python", "args": ["-m", "earshot", "mcp"],
  "env": {"EARSHOT_THREADS": "3"}}}}
```

Models load on the first call and stay warm. On a slow machine start Claude Code with `MCP_TIMEOUT=60000`. The
optional `llm_critique` tool reads `GEMINI_API_KEY` from the environment; never write a literal key into a file.

### Python

```python
import earshot
earshot.describe('whoosh.wav')
earshot.find('typing.ogg', 'a single isolated key press')
earshot.timeline('soundtrack.wav', video='film.mp4')
from earshot import api   # everything in one namespace: api.rank, api.critique, api.realness_many, ...
```

## Agent skills

Two skills ship in `skills/`. Copy or symlink them into `~/.claude/skills/` (or a project's `.claude/skills/`).

- **`skills/earshot`**: how an agent should listen with earshot: which command answers which question, how to read
  the verdicts, when not to trust them.
- **`skills/real-sound`**: a full process for premium, realistic soundtracks for code-made films from real licensed
  recordings: sourcing with licence checks, a music edit, a JSON sound design, a deterministic mixer, measured QA, a
  multi-lens critique, mastering, credits and mux. earshot chooses, trims and verifies the sounds.

## How good is it?

Every number below comes with the command that measured it in [docs/VALIDATION.md](docs/VALIDATION.md). What
earshot cannot judge is in [docs/LIMITS.md](docs/LIMITS.md).

- **Matching descriptions** (a held-out library of 125 real recordings, nothing tuned on it): in a library search a
  "strong" verdict is the right kind of sound 98% of the time and the exact variant 61% of the time.
- **Finding the moment**: on a recording of 17 single key presses the found trims land on real key presses; in a
  300 s scene every planted event is found as a tight trim.
- **Real vs code-synthesized**: held-out ROC-AUC 0.92 with whole sound families held out. Firm verdicts call 6.7% of
  real clips synthesized and 5.5% of synthesized clips real; a fifth of clips get "uncertain".
- **Listening through a soundtrack**: 93% of the sound effects placed in a 60 s film mix are detected as events (89%
  of the quiet ones under music). A 60-90 s film takes about 1.5 minutes on a laptop CPU.
- **Launch scorecard**: each reference film critiqued against the other six falls in range on 86% of the metrics
  (the no-overfit baseline is about 71%; some rules changed after the first run, so it is not a blind test).

## Limits

earshot hears through two open models and a set of measurements. Trustworthy: loudness, timing and sync to picture,
"is this the kind of sound I asked for" on single exposed sounds, picking among candidates, obvious code-synthesized
sources. Hints only: tags of events inside a busy mix, music genre and mood. It cannot judge taste or emotion,
provenance or licences, speech content, or anything above 14 kHz from the models. The launch scorecard describes the
style of the 7 films behind it, not every good film. Details in [docs/LIMITS.md](docs/LIMITS.md).

## Repo map

```
earshot/            the package: CLI, Python API, MCP server, CPU model wrappers
  forge/            make sounds in code: DSP building blocks, critic, model-free tone checks, search, recipes/
    fit/            recording -> code: modal / sines / spectral fitters, quality metrics, recipe codegen
    bank/, kits/    the sound bank (render blocks + fingerprints, no audio) and the kit presets: earshot sfx / kit
  gallery.py        the static listening page
  data/             vocabulary + calibration stats, realness model weights, launch profile (numbers only, no media)
skills/earshot/     agent skill: how to listen with earshot
skills/real-sound/  agent skill: real-recordings soundtracks (scripts, templates, prompts, references)
docs/               VALIDATION, LIMITS, FORGE_V2, FIT, SFX, the motion-SFX study, launch-video playbook, design notes
eval/               evaluation scripts and results per area (see eval/README.md)
tests/              pytest (fast by default; --slow loads the models)
```

No audio or video is stored in this repo. The evaluation data (licensed recordings and third-party films) is not
redistributed; only derived numbers are committed.

## Licence

MIT for the code (see [LICENSE](LICENSE)). The models are downloaded from their authors under their own licences:
CLAP (`laion/larger_clap_general`) Apache-2.0, AST (`MIT/ast-finetuned-audioset-10-10-0.4593`) BSD-3-Clause.
`skills/real-sound/scripts/master.py` is vendored from the Cinetic skill by the same author.

items.readme:
# Handwired

Turn your regular JavaScript code into a neural net; no training, exact, yet also fully differentiable!

## How It Works

A program's made of if-else, loops, and state. Handwired transforms them into matrix multiplication + reglu over floats. For example:

```ts
const a = 5
const result = (a > 4) ? 10 : 12
```

The above can be expressed as basic arithmetic:

```ts
const a = 5
// Math.max(0, x) is ReLU. For an integer a, above4 is 1 if a > 4, and 0 otherwise
const above4 = Math.max(0, a - 4) - Math.max(0, a - 5)
// Both branches compute, and above4 picks one
const result = above4 * 10 + (1 - above4) * 12
```

You can calculate that by hand and see that both arrive at the same result.

We then collect the + and * and relu into a giant matmul, and either run it on JS or WebGPU, for fun.

Because we basically only use these 2 primitives:
- the full program stays differentiable
- the weights don't need training since they're written manually
- existing gpu techniques, such as fusion, sparsity, reordering, have a great time optimizing such minimal primitives

This unlocks lots of funny use-cases, like:
- unfreezing the weights and train them (what does that even do? Let's find out!)
- attaching a specific frozen program to a generic neural net and train end-to-end (now a nanoGPT can do both Shakespeare and your particular UI?)
- achieving GPU-level of parallelism with JS code that was written in a traditional single-threaded way (see the JSON search demo that runs in milliseconds over 100k documents)

## Play With It

Try the demos live: https://chenglou.me/handwired/

`git clone && bun install`, then `bun start` to run them locally. Check `docs/`, `src/` and `template/` to get started! (`lab/` is a bunch of old experiments you can check or ignore)

![HandwiredOS](assets/demos-handwiredos.webp)

**Uncharted 1, 2 and 3 from the PS4 collection running natively on Windows 10 and 11, by [SuperMedo](https://github.com/Supermedo).** Mohammed Albarghouthi

Same idea as my [Bloodborne port](https://github.com/Supermedo/bloodborne_pc): the original PS4 game
code runs directly on your PC and the graphics are translated to Vulkan. Unpack the zip, start
`Uncharted.exe`, pick your game folder, choose a game and press **PLAY**.

**[Download the latest version](https://github.com/Supermedo/uncharted_pc/releases/latest)** · **[Join the Discord]([https://discord.gg/yTMG8c4Bqm](https://discord.gg/s3RgH6cRfJ))**

> **No game files are included.** You need your own decrypted dump of the collection
> (CUSA02343, CUSA02320, ...: the folder with eboot.bin, big2-ps4_Shipping.elf,
> big3-ps4_Shipping.elf, sce_sys, u1data, u2data and u3data).
> This project is not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment or Naughty Dog.

## Features

- All three games from one launcher: Drake's Fortune, Among Thieves and Drake's Deception.
- 60 FPS like on PS4, or 120 FPS (higher rates are experimental).
- Anti-aliasing with TAA, AMD FSR 3.1, AMD FSR 4 or NVIDIA DLSS (DLAA).
- Frame generation: AMD FSR 3 (any GPU) or NVIDIA DLSS (RTX 40 2x, RTX 50 up to 4x).
- Keyboard, mouse and controller together, all remappable. Mouse look in U3.
- Add to Steam and desktop shortcuts from the launcher, automatic updates.

## Requirements

- Windows 10 (1903 or later) or Windows 11, 64-bit.
- A graphics card with Vulkan 1.3 and a current driver.
- About 8 GB of free memory (RAM + page file).

## Known problems

- **Uncharted 3, Cartagena square (chapter 2):** at high frame rates (240 Hz setting, ~80 FPS)
  the game could freeze and close with "GPU crash: the graphics device was lost". It came from
  the speed fix for that area and is fixed in 0.3. If it still happens to you, set Frame rate to
  60 on the Display page and open an issue with your `user\last_run.log`.
- **Uncharted 3:** green or black shapes flash for a single frame on some characters (Sully's
  shirt in Cartagena). It happens in shadPS4 too, so it's a shader translation problem. Not fixed yet.
- **Crash with "ASSERTION: GetRenderFrameParams(frameToFreeInstancesFor)->m_gfxEopTick":** the
  game got too many frames ahead of the GPU side while it was busy (building shaders on a first
  run). 0.3.1 holds the game at most one frame ahead, like on PS4. If you still see it, open an
  issue with your log.
- Frame rates above 120 are experimental.

## Building

MSYS2 CLANG64 on Windows: `bash build.sh` builds `out\bb-probe.exe`, and
`bash packaging/windows/package.sh` makes `dist\uncharted-windows` and the zip.

## Credits

Built on [bbport](https://github.com/deadinside28/bloodborne_pc), the native Linux port of
Bloodborne by deadinside28, and on the [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4)
renderer. Video decoding (Videodec2) and the DLSS bridge come from
[IFreemz/shadPS4-Bloodborne-DLSS-FSR](https://github.com/IFreemz/shadPS4-Bloodborne-DLSS-FSR).
Thanks to Mindro for the shadPS4 Uncharted build that showed which problems to look for.

Also used: [FSR-Vulkan](https://github.com/FireBurn/FSR-Vulkan) and the AMD FidelityFX SDK (FSR),
FSR 4 assets from [FireBurn/Q2RTX](https://github.com/FireBurn/Q2RTX), the

# 中国初中数学（七—九年级）知识图谱 · 第一版草稿

用「知识点节点 + 先修边」的有向无环图（DAG）描述人教版初中数学（七上至九下）的知识结构，数据格式参考 [Marble os-taxonomy](https://github.com/withmarbleapp/os-taxonomy)（`topics` + `dependencies`）。

> **状态声明：这是 AI 生成的初稿，未经任何教师审核。**
> 知识点的拆分粒度、掌握标准、诊断题答案，尤其是**先修关系（哪些是 hard、哪些是 soft，甚至某条边该不该存在）都需要一线初中数学教师审核**后才能用于教学、诊断或学习路径推荐。诊断题答案虽经抽查心算，但没有逐题由人工复核。

## 数据来源与对齐依据

- **课程标准**：教育部《义务教育数学课程标准（2022年版）》第四学段（7—9 年级）的内容范围与学段要求（数与代数、图形与几何、统计与概率、综合与实践四个领域）。第三轮起，课标第四学段【内容要求】已拆成机器可读条目（`data/cn-curriculum-standards.json`，157 条），每个正式知识点通过 `standards` 字段挂接 1–3 条（共 383 条映射）；来源、规则、覆盖率与局限见 [docs/standards-mapping.md](docs/standards-mapping.md)。
- **教材顺序**：人民教育出版社（人教版）义务教育教科书数学，**采用 2024 年审定的新版**。章节目录取自第三方电子课本目录站 dzskb.com（非人教社官方页面），核对情况如下：

  | 册次 | 采用的目录 | 核实情况 |
  |---|---|---|
  | 七上 | 第一章 有理数 … 第六章 几何图形初步 | 已核对目录页 |
  | 七下 | 第七章 相交线与平行线 … 第十二章 数据的收集、整理与描述 | 已核对目录页 |
  | 八上 | 第十三章 三角形 … 第十八章 分式（2024 审定版） | 已核对目录页 |
  | 八下 | 第十九章 二次根式 … 第二十四章 数据的分析（2024 审定版） | 已核对目录页 |
  | 九上 | 第二十五章 一元二次方程 … 第三十章 直线与圆的位置关系（2024 审定版） | 已核对目录页 |
  | 九下 | 第三十一章 相似；第三十二章 锐角三角函数（章末综合与实践：停车设计问题）；第三十三章 投影与视图（章末综合与实践：建筑中的数学）；第三十四章 随机事件的概率（34.1.1 随机事件，34.1.2 概率，34.2 用列举法求概率，34.3 用频率估计概率） | **非官方、待核**，详见下方「九下目录的来源与核实情况」 |

  新版教材相对旧版有较大调整（如多边形移入八下“四边形”、反比例函数移入九上、新增“数据的四分位数”“综合与实践”主题、概率由九上移到九下并改名“随机事件的概率”等），本图谱按新版目录处理。

### 九下目录的来源与核实情况（查证日期：2026-10-17；**非官方、待核**）

**结论**：没有找到人教社（pep.com.cn）官方发布的 2024 版九下目录页（官方“新教材介绍”页只介绍编写思路，未列各册章目；pep.com.cn 的“数学 九年级下册”页是旧版封面，页面不显示目录）。九下的 2024 版教材预计 2027 年春季学期才开始使用。下列目录是综合第三方来源后的**最可靠推定**，并非官方原文，章名、章号请以教材实物或人教社官方目录为准。

| 章 | 采用的章名 | 依据 |
|---|---|---|
| 第三十一章 | 相似 | 来源 A（搜索摘要）；与来源 D 的九上末章“第三十章”衔接 |
| 第三十二章 | 锐角三角函数；章末“综合与实践：停车设计问题” | 来源 A（搜索摘要） |
| 第三十三章 | 投影与视图；章末“综合与实践：建筑中的数学” | 来源 A（搜索摘要） |
| 第三十四章 | 随机事件的概率：34.1.1 随机事件、34.1.2 概率、34.2 用列举法求概率、34.3 用频率估计概率 | 来源 B、C |

来源：
- A：知乎专栏《2024年秋季学期修订人教版初中数学7-9年级教材目录》https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/706262283 。正文需登录无法读取，**只看到搜索结果摘要**：“九年级下册：第三十一章相似 第三十二章锐角三角函数 综合与实践：停车设计问题 第三十三章投影与视图 综合与实践：建筑中的数学 第三十四章随机……”（摘要在此截断）。
- B：LibreMath 教辅页 https://libremath.cn/textbook/renjiao-jiuxia-sui-ji-shi-jian-de-gai-lv/ ，标称“人教版（2024 审定）九年级下册第三十四章《随机事件的概率》”，列出 34.1.1—34.3 各小节，并说明 2027 春起使用、章名由“概率初步”改为“随机事件的概率”。第三方教辅，非官方。
- C：21cnjy 新教材九下页的搜索摘要（https://mip.21cnjy.com/mulu/7/326226-2.html ，页面本身抓取超时）：“第三十四章随机事件的概率 34.1 随机事件与概率 34.2 用列举法求概率 ……”，与 B 一致。
- D：电子课本网 dzskb.com 的九上 2024 页 https://www.dzskb.com/rjbsx9sc-2024.html ，九上为第二十五至第三十章（反比例函数已在九上第二十七章），所以九下从第三十一章起，与 A 衔接。

**未采用的来源**：dzskb.com 标为“2024 审定版（现行）”的九下页 https://www.dzskb.com/rjbsx9sce-2024.html 列出的是“第二十六章 反比例函数 / 二十七 相似 / 二十八 锐角三角函数 / 二十九 投影与视图”，与同站旧版页内容完全相同，且与它自己的九上 2024 页矛盾（反比例函数不可能同时在九上第二十七章和九下第二十六章），判断为误标的旧版目录，不采用。

**仍待核的部分**：(1) 第三十一至三十三章的**小节号**没有查到，`chapter` 字段只写到章，不写小节号；第三十四章小节号来自 B、C。(2) “综合与实践”两项只来自来源 A 的摘要，活动的具体内容未核实，`cnm_290`、`cnm_291` 的描述与先修边是按主题名推定的。(3) 章内知识点是沿用第一版的拆分，没有逐节对照新教材。(4) 第三十四章章名“随机事件的概率”来自 B、C 两个第三方来源，来源 A 的摘要被截断。
- **小学先修**：18 个外部节点（`cnm_ext_*`）按小学数学课程内容概括，只作为图的根，不展开其内部结构。
- **格式参考**：已阅读 Marble 的 `data/topics.json` / `data/dependencies.json`（节点含 `type`、`domain`、`evidence`、`assessmentPrompt`；边为 `topicId` 依赖 `prerequisiteId`）。其中文分支 [os-taxonomy-beijing](https://github.com/luw2007/os-taxonomy-beijing) 只读了 README，**没有解析它的数据文件**。本项目在字段含义上对应关系为：`mastery_criteria` ≈ `evidence`，`diagnostic_question` ≈ `assessmentPrompt`；但文件顶层是裸数组（没有 `version`/`topicCount` 包装），id 为 `cnm_NNN`，也没有 `centrality`、`ageRange`、`standards`。

## 文件

```
data/topics.json         知识点节点（JSON 数组）
data/dependencies.json   先修边（JSON 数组）
data/cn-curriculum-standards.json  课标第四学段内容要求条目（157 条）
docs/standards-mapping.md          课标对齐说明：来源、映射规则、覆盖率、未映射清单、局限
data/questions.json      题库：每个正式知识点 4–5 题（共 1407 题）
data/verification_report.json  题库答案核验报告（自动核验 + 独立第二遍复核）
data/second_pass_log.json      第二遍复核的裁决与修正记录；data/_second_pass/ 是解题者的原始答案和推导
docs/questions.md                题库格式、核验方法、统计、局限
scripts/validate.py      校验脚本（仅标准库；含题库检查）
scripts/verify_questions.py  题库答案自动核验（受限表达式求值）
scripts/second_pass.py       独立第二遍复核的辅助脚本（出盲解题、比对答案）
CHANGELOG.md             按日期记录的变更日志（含 id 变动说明）
index.html               单文件浏览页面（无外部依赖）
diagnose/                诊断小工具（纯静态：index.html、engine.js、app.js、style.css、README.md）
tests/test_engine.js     诊断引擎测试（Node，无依赖）
scripts/screenshot.js    无头 Chrome 冒烟测试与截图脚本
screenshots/             诊断小工具截图（01-start / 02-question / 03-result / 04-graph / 05-explanation）
```

### topics.json 字段

正式知识点（`external: false`）：

| 字段 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `id` | 稳定 id，`cnm_001` … |
| `name` | 中文名称 |
| `domain` | 数与代数 / 图形与几何 / 统计与概率 / 综合与实践 |
| `grade` | 7 / 8 / 9（整数） |
| `semester` | "上" 或 "下" |
| `chapter` | 人教版章节，如 `七上 第一章 有理数 1.2.1` |
| `type` | conceptual / procedural / reasoning / application / modeling |
| `description` | 通俗说明（1—2 句） |
| `mastery_criteria` | 2—3 条掌握标准（字符串数组） |
| `diagnostic_question` | `{"question": "...", "answer": "..."}` |
| `external` | `false` |
| `standards` | 课标映射数组，元素 `{"id", "confidence", "note"?}`，见下节；可为空数组 |
| `root_reason` | 仅当非外部节点没有任何先修边时必填（本版没有这样的节点，见下） |

外部（小学先修）节点：只有 `id`、`name`、`domain`、`grade`（固定为 `"小学"`）、`description`、`external: true`，另有 `standards: []`（本版没有做第三学段课标条目）。

说明：
- 数学里函数归“数与代数”，点的坐标、图形变换归“图形与几何”（与课标领域划分一致）。
- “综合与实践”节点（如 `设计学校田径运动会比赛场地`）是教材中的主题活动，按 `modeling` 处理，诊断题只是对活动中某一数学要点的检查。
- `一元二次方程根与系数的关系（拓展）`：课标要求“了解”（例67），第三轮已据此更正描述；名称里的“（拓展）”保留，其是否作为必学请教师判断。

### dependencies.json 字段

```json
{"topicId": "A", "prerequisiteId": "B", "strength": "hard", "reason": "一句中文理由"}
```

含义：**A 依赖 B**（学 A 之前需要 B）。

- `hard`：不会 B 基本无法学 A；`soft`：会 B 对学 A 明显有帮助（类比、简化、背景），但不是硬门槛。**这个区分是 AI 的主观判断，未经审核。**
- 只保留直接先修关系，并做了传递约简：`hard` 边仅在存在另一条全 `hard` 路径时才被删除，`soft` 边在存在任何其他路径时即被删除（生成时共剔除 90 条冗余边）。因此若看到某条边“缺失”，通常是已经能由更近的先修推出。
- 由于每个正式知识点最终都能追溯到至少一个小学外部节点，**本版没有需要 `root_reason` 的根节点**；图的根全部是 `cnm_ext_*`。

## 当前统计（`python3 scripts/validate.py` 实际输出）

- 知识点总数 **333**：正式 **315**，小学外部 **18**
- 按领域（正式）：数与代数 142，图形与几何 117，统计与概率 **43**，综合与实践 13
- 按册次（正式）：七上 61，七下 58，八上 57，八下 57，九上 49，九下 33
- 按类型（正式）：conceptual 102，procedural 101，reasoning 58，modeling 31，application 23
- 先修边 **616** 条：hard 497，soft 119；其中 53 条指向小学外部节点；正式知识点平均 1.92 条先修
- 未被任何知识点依赖的末端节点 63 个

## 第二轮迭代（2026-10-17）改了什么

详见 `CHANGELOG.md`。要点：

1. **九下章目核实**：去掉所有“（暂拟）”，九下 `chapter` 改为第三十一至三十四章的实际章名（来源与“非官方、待核”说明见上）。原九下 22 个知识点的 id 全部不变；章名由“概率初步”改为“随机事件的概率”，并给概率各点补上 34.1.1/34.1.2/34.2/34.3 小节号。新增两个章末“综合与实践”（`cnm_290` 停车设计问题、`cnm_291` 建筑中的数学）。
2. **统计与概率加厚**：领域“统计与概率”正式知识点由 **20 增至 43**（新增 23）。分布：七下 17、八下 12、九下 14。七上、八上、九上在新版教材里没有统计与概率章，所以没有硬凑。另有 3 个相关的“综合与实践”（`cnm_109`、`cnm_218` 原有，`cnm_315` 新增），不计入上面的 43。
3. **边**：新增 50 条（含统计新点的先修边及 `cnm_288`←`cnm_297` 等连接原有统计点的边），删除 1 条冗余边（`cnm_288`←`cnm_106`，已可经新增的 `cnm_297` 到达）；原有 287 条理由少于 8 个汉字的边，再加 79 条仍只有短语的边，共 366 条理由改写成完整一句话（最短的也有 9 个汉字以上）。
4. 没有改动 `scripts/validate.py`。

## 课标对齐（第三轮）

- **课标条目**：`data/cn-curriculum-standards.json`，教育部《义务教育数学课程标准（2022年版）》第四学段【内容要求】共 **157** 条：数与代数 49、图形与几何 92、统计与概率 13、综合与实践 3。id 形如 `cms-2022:4.NA.01`（NA 数与代数、GG 图形与几何、SP 统计与概率、IP 综合与实践），条文是课标原文，来自教育部官网 PDF。
- **知识点映射**：每个正式知识点的 `standards` 数组为 `{"id": "cms-2022:4.NA.17", "confidence": "exact"|"inferred", "note": "..."}`；exact 表示条款正文直接点名，inferred 表示前提、特例、延伸或教材细化，必须写 note。
- **覆盖率**：315 个正式知识点中 **313 个（99.4%）** 有映射；2 个未映射（`cnm_130` 辅助线与模型、`cnm_192` 折叠与动点问题）。另有 15 条课标条款没有对应知识点（多为作图、欣赏类和选学内容），列在文档里。
- **全部说明**（来源与 URL、检索日期、映射规则、覆盖率、未映射清单、已知局限）见 [docs/standards-mapping.md](docs/standards-mapping.md)。映射由 AI 生成，未经课程专家审核。
- 小学外部节点的 `standards` 为空数组，没有建第三学段（`cms-2022:3.*`）条目。
- `STRICT_STANDARDS=1 python3 scripts/validate.py` 会把“正式知识点 standards 为空”当作错误；默认只打印警告。

## 统计与概率知识点的教材落册（第二轮后）

- 七下 第十二章（17 个）：调查方式与样本（`cnm_102`—`cnm_104`、`cnm_298`、`cnm_299`、`cnm_300`），数据整理与统计图（`cnm_105`、`cnm_292`—`cnm_297`），直方图与趋势图（`cnm_106`—`cnm_108`、`cnm_301`）。
- 八下 第二十四章（12 个）：平均数、加权平均数、中位数、众数、方差、四分位数、分组数据及新增的样本估计总体、极端值、方差比较、箱线图。
- 九下 第三十四章（14 个）：随机事件、概率意义、列举法、列表法与树状图、频率估计概率、游戏公平性，以及新增的可能性排序、概率性质、等可能判断、放回与不放回、三步树状图、实际估计、统计图表综合、误解辨析。
- 小节号（如 12.1.2、24.2）是按第一版已有标注推定的，没有逐节核对新教材。新增的 `cnm_305`（箱线图）是否为教材必学内容、`cnm_315`（用随机试验检验游戏的公平性）是补充课题，均已在描述里标明，请教师取舍。

## 诊断小工具（第四轮；第五轮改为每个知识点最多 2 题）

`diagnose/` 是一个基于上述数据的静态、可离线的诊断页面：选一个目标知识点（或整个章节），按先修关系自适应出题（第一题答对则掌握并跳过全部祖先；答错则再出一道同级或更容易的题——第二题也错才算薄弱并回溯到先修，hard 先于 soft；第二题答对标为「不稳」，不回溯），给出薄弱的根因、不稳的知识点、按拓扑序排列的学习路径、相关课标条目原文和一张纯 SVG 路径图；每题作答后显示解析和参考答案；进度保存在 localStorage，可导出 JSON 或打印。核心算法与判题在 `diagnose/engine.js`（纯函数，浏览器与 Node 通用），由 `node tests/test_engine.js` 测试。

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
# 访问 http://localhost:8000/diagnose/            （演示：?target=cnm_221&demo=1）
node tests/test_engine.js                          # 引擎测试
node scripts/screenshot.js                         # 冒烟测试 + 截图（需要本机 Chrome）
```

算法说明、判题规则、URL 参数与局限见 [diagnose/README.md](diagnose/README.md)；浏览页 `index.html` 右上角也有入口。每个知识点最多问 2 题，诊断结果只是线索。

## 题库（第五轮）

`data/questions.json`：给 315 个正式知识点各建 4–5 道题，**共 1407 题**；`topics.json` 里原有的 `diagnostic_question` 迁移为每个知识点的第 1 题（id 后缀 `_q1`），原字段保留不动。

| 统计 | 数量 |
|---|---|
| 按 type | numeric 903，choice 475，short 23，self 6（numeric + choice 占 97.9%） |
| 按 difficulty | basic 591，standard 537，advanced 279（每个知识点都含 basic 和 standard） |
| 每知识点题数 | 最少 4，最多 5，平均 4.47（4 题 × 168，5 题 × 147） |
| 自动核验（`verify` 表达式） | 875 题通过，mismatch 0，unverifiable 532（主要是文字选项的选择题） |
| 独立第二遍复核 | 1401 题盲解比对，原始不一致 3 处（全是解题者算错），发现并修正答案错误 0 处，另改 4 处含糊题干 + 1 处错误解析；`second_pass_mismatch` = 0 |

```bash
python3 scripts/verify_questions.py   # 自动核验，写 data/verification_report.json；mismatch 为 0 才打印 VERIFICATION PASSED
python3 scripts/validate.py           # 含题库格式检查与题量统计
```

题目与答案全部由 AI 生成、未经教师审核，复核者与出题者是同一模型家族；格式、核验方法、统计与局限见 [docs/questions.md](docs/questions.md)。

## 已知局限

- **审核缺位**：见开头状态声明；先修关系、hard/soft 强度、诊断题难度与区分度都没有经过教师或学生数据检验。
- **覆盖不均**：统计与概率现为 43 个，但全部集中在七下、八下、九下三册（新教材只在这三册安排统计与概率，不含七上、八上、九上）；九下目录为第三方来源推定，非官方、待核（见上）；教材中的“阅读与思考”“数学活动”“小结”“信息技术应用”等栏目没有单独成点，仅少数“综合与实践”“探究与发现”并入。
- **粒度不统一**：个别知识点（如各类应用题）按题型归并，个别（如三角形全等的各判定）拆得较细，需按实际教学再调。
- **题库很小**：每个知识点 4–5 题、诊断时最多问 2 题，题与答案由 AI 生成、未经教师审核，难度与干扰项没有学生数据校准，不能代替完整测评。
- **按教材顺序推断**：部分先修边（如命题、定理类内容）反映的是教材编排而非严格逻辑依赖，已尽量标为 `soft`。

## 运行校验

```bash
python3 scripts/validate.py
```

检查：JSON 合法；id 唯一；必填字段齐全；`domain`/`type`/`strength` 取值合法；每条边的两端都存在；无自环、无重复边；无环（有环时打印环路）；每个非外部知识点要么有先修边要么有 `root_reason`；没有完全孤立的节点。并打印按领域、按册次的数量以及边数、hard/soft 数。第三轮新增：`standards` 引用的课标 id 必须存在于 `data/cn-curriculum-standards.json`，`confidence` 只能是 `exact`/`inferred`，课标文件自身的 id 格式与编号连续性；并打印课标条目数、映射覆盖率；正式知识点 `standards` 为空时只打印警告（至多 30 个），设置 `STRICT_STANDARDS=1` 才视为错误。全部通过时输出 `VALIDATION PASSED` 且退出码为 0，否则输出错误并以非 0 退出。

## 打开浏览页面

页面通过 `fetch` 读取 `data/*.json`，浏览器不允许直接用 `file://` 打开，请在本目录启动一个静态服务器：

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
# 然后访问 http://localhost:8000/
```

功能：左侧可按学科、年级/册次、类型筛选并搜索（名称、描述、章节）；可勾选是否显示小学先修节点。点击知识点后显示描述、掌握标准、诊断题（答案默认折叠）、**先修链**（向上递归，树状或分层列表两种视图，边上标注硬/软先修及理由），以及**它是哪些后续知识点的先修**。地址栏 `#cnm_219` 形式的 hash 可直接定位到某个知识点。

## 后续建议

1. 请初中数学教师先审先修边（尤其是 hard 边），并用教材实物或人教社官方目录核对九下的章名、章号和小节号。
2. 请课程专家审核 `standards` 映射（尤其 inferred），并考虑为 15 条无对应知识点的课标条款补点；再补充每个知识点的常见错误、典型例题。
3. 用真实学生答题数据校准诊断题与先修强度。

items.readme:
Git designed for AI agents.

Anthropic built **Scion**, a faster version control system for coding agents, and described it in [Redesigning source control](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/redesigning-source-control): a server-centric system built for hundreds of agents that read, write and land code at the same time. Scion is internal to Anthropic and is not available to the public. So I built **gitai**: an open-source version of that design that anyone can run, and that the community can improve and maintain together. MIT licensed. Vendor neutral: the server never calls a language model, and every AI feature works with any provider, or none. gitai is an independent implementation of the publicly described design. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. --- ## Why Classic Git hosting was built for humans who clone a repository, work for hours and push once. Coding agents work differently: thousands of short-lived tasks, each touching a few files, each wanting to land in seconds, all on the same branches. Full clones, merge queues and client-side history walks become the bottleneck. Scion's answer is to move the work to the server: clients stay online and fetch only what they need, history questions are answered (and cached) by the server, changes land through a compare-and-swap instead of a queue, every update is an entry in a changeset log, and the repository state lives in a consistent database plus object storage so servers scale out. gitai implements these ideas, with normal Git repositories underneath. ## The Scion ideas, implemented | Scion idea | In gitai | |---|---| | **Always-online clients** that fetch exactly what they need | `ObjectService` serves single objects and sparse trees; `graft clone` and `graft sparse` materialize only the paths you ask for. | | **Source control as an API**: history runs on the server | Blame, path history, ancestry and code search run server-side and are memoized as derived data, computed once per commit. | | **Landing without a merge queue** | `UserLand` rebases a change onto the current tip and lands it with a compare-and-swap; concurrent lands on one branch are batched into a single reference update. | | **Automatic conflict resolution** | A conflicting land is resolved by a resolver you choose (any LLM provider, a deterministic tool, or none) through a versioned, vendor-neutral protocol. | | **Changeset log** | Every accepted reference update is recorded with its operation and actor in a dense, ordered log that clients list or watch live. | | **Storage core: a database and object storage, stateless servers** | Each change is a changeset in a write-ahead log in SQLite or PostgreSQL, with a compare-and-swap per reference; packs live in object storage (file, S3, GCS, Azure). Server nodes are caches that any node can rebuild, so you add nodes to scale. | | **Test after landing, revert the culprit** | `graft-verify` tests the tip, bisects a failure and reverts the change that broke it. | | **Monitoring agents ("superfans")** | Agents follow the changeset stream and report what matters to each component, also through Slack. | | **Agent-friendly review** | Reviews with semantic approval rules: a comment-only change can need fewer approvals than a logic change. | | **Agents as first-class users** | Per-agent tokens, an RPC allowlist and branch policies decide what each agent may do. | | **Strict cache tiers** | `graft-cache` caches immutable objects in daemon and regional tiers, verifying every object. | ## Architecture ``` agents, CI jobs, sparse workspaces graft CLI / Go SDK | v gRPC +-------------------------------------------------+ | graft-cache (optional daemon and cache tiers) | +------------------------+------------------------+ v +---------------------------------------------------------------+ | gitai server (any number of nodes) | | land - objects - changesets - derived data - search - review | | write path: changeset + compare-and-swap per reference | +-----------+--------------------------------+------------------+ | | v v +-----------------------+ +-----------------------------+ | SQLite / PostgreSQL | | object storage | | changeset WAL, refs, | | content-addressed packs | | changelog, reviews | | (file, S3, GCS, Azure) | +-----------------------+ +-----------------------------+ \ / local Git repositories = caches any node can rebuild ``` Details: [ARCHITECTURE.md](doc/graft/ARCHITECTURE.md) and [STORAGE.md](doc/graft/STORAGE.md). ## Quick start Requirements: Linux or macOS, Go 1.26, a C toolchain, Meson and Ninja (the build compiles a bundled Git). ```shell git clone https://github.com/feder-cr/git-ai.git cd git-ai make build # server, CLI and tools into _build/bin examples/graft/quickstart.sh # a server, a cache daemon, two agents and a land, in a temporary directory ./_build/bin/graft # the CLI and its commands ``` To run your own server, adapt [`examples/graft/config.toml`](examples/graft/config.toml) and start it with `_build/bin/gitaly serve config.toml`. To put the repository state in a database and object storage, add a `[graft.storage]` section: start in `shadow` mode, import your repositories, then switch to `authoritative` ([STORAGE.md](doc/graft/STORAGE.md)). Inside the code the extensions are called **Graft**: the `[graft]` configuration section, the `graft` CLI, `internal/graft` and `doc/graft`. ## Documentation - [Quickstart](doc/graft/QUICKSTART.md) and [configuration reference](doc/graft/CONFIGURATION.md) - [Architecture](doc/graft/ARCHITECTURE.md) and the [storage core](doc/graft/STORAGE.md) - [Landing and batching](doc/graft/LAND-BATCHING.md), [conflict resolution](doc/graft/RESOLVE.md), [derived data](doc/graft/DERIVED.md) - [Review](doc/graft/REVIEW.md), [search](doc/graft/SEARCH.md), [verification](doc/graft/VERIFY.md), [superfans](doc/graft/SUPERFAN.md) and [Slack chat](doc/graft/SUPERFAN-CHAT.md) - [Agent security](doc/graft/AGENT-SECURITY.md), [benchmarks](doc/graft/BENCH.md), [fuzzing](doc/graft/FUZZING.md) - [Limitations and roadmap](doc/graft/LIMITATIONS.md) - Design documents of each phase: [PLAN.md](doc/graft/PLAN.md) to [PLAN6.md](doc/graft/PLAN6.md) ## Status Version 0.1.0, the first public release. Everything above is implemented and covered by unit, end-to-end, multi-node, crash and fuzz tests. Interfaces may still change before 1.0. Known gaps (for example garbage collection of packs in the storage core) are listed in [LIMITATIONS.md](doc/graft/LIMITATIONS.md). ## Community gitai is meant to be maintained by its community. Open an issue to report a bug or propose an idea, start a discussion before a large design change, and send pull requests: tests and a short description of the reasoning make them easy to review. The design documents in `doc/graft/PLAN*.md` explain why things are the way they are. ## Credits and license gitai is MIT licensed, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). It started as a fork of [Gitaly](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitaly), GitLab's Git RPC server (MIT, Copyright GitLab Inc.), which provides the Git plumbing underneath; every upstream Gitaly RPC keeps working. The non-MIT `ee/` directory of upstream Gitaly is not part of this repository. Gitaly's own README is kept in [doc/UPSTREAM-GITALY.md](doc/upstream/README-GITALY.md), and third-party notices are in [NOTICE](NOTICE).

items.readme:
# Free My TV **A fast, ad-free home screen for Google TV, LG and Samsung TVs.** Trending picks from your own apps, the weather at a glance, and a look that follows the sunset.
Open source. Built with Claude Code. One button to undo. [**freemytv.io**](https://freemytv.io) · [Install](#install) · [LG TVs](#lg-tvs-webos) · [Samsung TVs](#samsung-tvs-tizen) · [Any TV](#any-tv) · [Make it yours](#make-it-yours)
## What you get - **No ads.** No sponsored rows, banners or autoplaying promos. Not one. - **Your apps, front and center.** The streaming apps you actually use, on a glass shelf. Pick them and their order right on the TV. - **Trending, not sponsored.** Three fresh picks every hour from what's trending this week and the latest releases, only from apps you already have. Movies and Shows get their own tabs. - **Weather and markets, one press away.** The hour-by-hour forecast, sunrise and sunset, and live crypto prices. - **Light by day, dark by night.** It follows your city's real sunset, the way your phone does. - **A screensaver to match.** Full-screen photos of the picks with a big glass clock. - **Fast.** 60 fps, every frame in 16.6 ms, on the TV's own chip. The home screen uses 96 MB of memory instead of 242 MB (−60%).
Measured on a 98″ TCL Google TV running Android 14. - **Set up on the TV.** Language, your city, temperature, theme, the weather and prices cards, which coins, and the apps on the shelf, in Free My TV's own settings. - **Safe.** No root. Nothing is uninstalled. One button brings back the factory home screen. ## Install About ten minutes. You need a Google TV or Android TV (Android 9 or newer) and a computer on the same Wi-Fi. ### The easy way: Claude Code 1. **On the TV**, turn on developer mode: Settings → System → About → press *Android TV OS build* 7 times. Then Settings → System → Developer options → turn on **USB debugging**. Write down the TV's IP address (Settings → Network & Internet). 2. **On your computer**, get the code: ```bash git clone https://github.com/simbasjungles/free-my-tv && cd free-my-tv ``` 3. **Open [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) in that folder** and say: > Install Free My TV on my TV at 192.168.1.50. I live in Lisbon. It installs the tools it needs, builds the app and puts it on your TV. Swap in your TV's IP and your city. 4. **On the TV**, open *Free My TV* → *Home Screen* → *Free My TV*, and accept the debugging prompt (tick *Always allow*). ### The manual way 1. **On the TV**, do step 1 above. 2. **Tools:** a JDK (17+), the Android SDK command-line tools (build-tools 34, platform android-34) and adb. On a Mac: ```bash brew install --cask temurin android-commandlinetools android-platform-tools sdkmanager "build-tools;34.0.0" "platforms;android-34" ``` On Linux, get OpenJDK 17, Android's command-line tools and adb from your package manager, then run the same `sdkmanager` line. On Windows, use WSL. 3. **Build:** ```bash ./build.sh ``` The first run creates `config.properties`. Set your city and your [TMDB key](#the-tmdb-key) there, then run it again. 4. **Install:** ```bash adb connect 192.168.1.50:5555 adb install -r FreeMyTV.apk ``` On TCL TVs, also let it run in the background (TCL blocks it by default, and the switch never starts): ```bash adb shell "appops set io.freemytv AUTO_START allow || appops set io.freemytv APP_AUTO_START allow" ``` 5. **On the TV**, open *Free My TV* → *Home Screen* → *Free My TV*. ## LG TVs (webOS) The same home screen as an LG app: the picks, the glass shelf with your apps, the drawer with inputs, weather and prices, day and night, Home Settings and the shelf editor. It installs through LG's own Developer Mode, with nothing rooted or changed on the TV. LG's home screen stays where it is, and Free My TV is one press of a number key away. You need an LG TV (webOS 3 or newer) and a computer on the same Wi-Fi, with Python 3. 1. **On the TV**, open the LG Content Store and install **Developer Mode**. Sign in with a free [LG developer account](https://webostv.developer.lge.com), turn on **Dev Mode Status** (the TV restarts), then turn on **Key Server**. Write down the IP address and the passphrase it shows. 2. **On your computer**, get the code and build. `config.properties` works as for Google TV (your city, your [TMDB key](#the-tmdb-key)): ```bash git clone https://github.com/simbasjungles/free-my-tv && cd free-my-tv python3 webos/build.py ``` 3. **Install.** The first time, it asks for the TV's passphrase; updates don't: ```bash python3 webos/install.py 192.168.1.50 ``` 4. **On the TV**, while Free My TV is open, hold a number key on the remote. From then on, that key opens it from anywhere. With Claude Code, say *"Install Free My TV on my LG TV at 192.168.1.50. I live in Lisbon."* It builds the app and hands you the install command, so you type the passphrase yourself. Developer Mode lasts about 40 days: open the Developer Mode app now and then and press **EXTEND**. To remove Free My TV, run `python3 webos/install.py 192.168.1.50 --uninstall`. ## Samsung TVs (Tizen) The same home screen as a Samsung app, with everything the LG one has: the picks, the shelf, the drawer with the inputs, the weather and the prices, day and night, and its own settings. It installs through Samsung's own Developer Mode, with nothing rooted or changed on the TV, and Samsung's home screen stays where it is. You need a Samsung TV from 2017 or newer (Tizen 3+) and a computer on the same Wi-Fi. 1. **On the TV**, open **Apps** and type `1 2 3 4 5` on the remote. Turn **Developer mode** on, type your computer's IP address in **Host PC IP**, and restart the TV. 2. **On your computer**, download [TizenBrew Installer](https://github.com/reisxd/TizenBrewInstaller/releases/latest), the community's installer for Samsung TVs, open it and connect to your TV. 3. **Install from GitHub:** type `simbasjungles/free-my-tv`. On 2023 and newer TVs it asks you to sign in to your Samsung account once, to sign the app for your TV. 4. **Straight to it:** in the TV's settings, under Start Screen Options, turn on **Autorun Last App**: the TV turns on into Free My TV. This build takes your city from the TV's time zone. For your exact city and the trending picks, build it with your own `config.properties` and [TMDB key](#the-tmdb-key): open the folder in Claude Code and say *"Install Free My TV on my Samsung TV at 192.168.1.50. I live in Lisbon."* It sets up Samsung's tools, and on 2023 and newer TVs you sign in to your Samsung account in the browser to make the certificate. ## Settings The first values come from `config.properties`, created by the first build (Google TV, LG and Samsung use the same file). Most of them can also be changed on the TV, in *Free My TV* → *Home Settings*, and the TV's choice wins: | Key | What it does | Default | |---|---|---| | `tmdb_key` | Your free TMDB key, for the picks | empty | | `tmdb_region` | Your country (two letters): which titles are on which app | `US` | | `latitude`, `longitude` | Your city, for the weather and the sunset | New York | | `city` | The name on the weather card | `Weather` | | `language` | `auto` (follows the TV), `en`, `es`, `pt`, `ru`, or `de` on Google TV | `auto` | | `show_crypto` | Show Binance crypto prices on home and screensaver | `true` | | `currency` | Crypto prices in `USD`, `EUR`, `BRL`… | `USD` | | `temperature` | `C`, `F` or `auto` | `auto` | | `disable_assistant` | Also turn off Google Assistant | `false` | Changed something? Run `./build.sh` and install again. Keep `freemytv.keystore`: updates are signed with it. ### The TMDB key Free, and it takes two minutes: create an account at [themoviedb.org](https://www.themoviedb.org/signup), then open [Settings → API](https://www.themoviedb.org/settings/api) and request a developer key. Paste the *API Read Access Token* (or the *API Key*) after `tmdb_key=`. It's your key: `config.properties` stays out of git. ## Going back On the TV: *Free My TV* → *Home Screen* → *Original*. The factory home screen, screensaver and every app come back exactly as they were. If the new home screen ever crashes three times in five minutes, it switches back by itself. To remove it for good, switch to *Original* first, then uninstall *Free My TV* (Settings → Apps). ## What it changes - It becomes the home screen and the screensaver. - It turns off, without uninstalling: - the stock home screen and screensaver; - Google TV's recovery home, Play Games and YouTube Music; - on TCL TVs, the TCL Channel, messages, store demo, hotel menu, manuals, mirroring and logging apps; - on Philco TVs, AI PONT (promo channels and app downloads) and the manual; - on Multilaser TVs, Anoki's screen-content recognition (ACR), the store demo and the manual; - Google Assistant, only with `disable_assistant=true`. - On TCL TVs, the remote's Netflix, YouTube and Prime buttons keep working through a small accessibility service that only reads those buttons. Pick what each one opens in *Free My TV* → *Remote Buttons*; *Original* turns the service off. - Picture, sound, inputs, remote pairing, Google services and the Play Store are on a protected list, checked before every change. - Apps that saved a Wi-Fi network are never turned off, since Android would erase the network. If the TV's first setup saved yours, the switch asks you to forget the network and connect again in Settings first (saved networks out of range don't show there; Claude Code can remove them). ## Any TV Free My TV runs on Google TV and Android TV: TCL, Sony, Hisense, Philips, Xiaomi and more, plus streamers like Chromecast with Google TV, the Google TV Streamer, onn 4K and NVIDIA Shield. And on [LG](#lg-tvs-webos) and [Samsung](#samsung-tvs-tizen) TVs, as an app. **Any other TV:** plug a Google TV streamer into HDMI and free that one. Same steps, same home screen. **A different brand or model:** ask Claude. Free My TV is made to be adapted by AI. Open the folder in Claude Code and say *"set it up for my Sony"*: it reads your TV, finds its home screen and its promo apps, updates the lists below and walks you through a test. [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) tells it how. | What | Where | |---|---| | Apps to turn off | `DEBLOAT` in [`HomeMode.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/HomeMode.java) | | Apps never to touch | `PROTECTED` in the same file | | Apps on the shelf | `SHELF` in [`HomeApps.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/HomeApps.java) | | Your brand's live TV app | `LIVE_TV_APPS` in the same file | ## Make it yours It's your code, and Claude Code finds its way around it. Try: - *"Add Crunchyroll to the shelf."* - *"Show the prices in euros."* - *"Add Spanish."* - *"Switch to the night look an hour after sunset."* ## How it works - **A plain Android app, no Gradle, no libraries.** [`build.sh`](build.sh) runs aapt2 → javac → d8 → zipalign → apksigner and makes a 2 MB APK. - **It uses the TV's own ADB, from inside the TV.** The app connects to `127.0.0.1:5555` with its own key (that's the *Allow USB debugging?* prompt) and runs the same commands you would: `cmd package set-home-activity`, `settings put secure screensaver_components`, `pm disable-user`. Nothing listens to the network. - **Drawn by hand on one Canvas**, with Android 13 shaders for the frosted glass and the sky (plain fills on Android 9 to 12, with lighter shadows and no GPU layers on 9 to 11 for their older GPUs). - **A safety net.** A watchdog in a separate process brings back the stock home screen after three crashes in five minutes, and a boot check keeps your choice after TV updates. - **On LG and Samsung, the same design in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript** ([`web/`](web)), written for the Chromium of older TVs, with no frameworks. [`webos/build.py`](webos/build.py) packs it with `config.properties` into an `.ipk` without LG's tools, and [`webos/install.py`](webos/install.py) installs it through Developer Mode; on LG it lists and opens apps through the TV's own service bus (Luna), as LG's launcher does. [`tizen/build.py`](tizen/build.py) packs the same app into a Samsung `.wgt`, which uses Tizen's web APIs for the apps and the inputs. To preview it on a computer: `python3 webos/build.py --preview`, then open `out/webos/index.html` (a stand-in lists sample apps). - **Data** from TMDB (trending titles, new releases and which app streams what in your country), Open-Meteo (forecast, sunrise and sunset), and optionally Binance (24-hour prices when `show_crypto=true`). | File | What it is | |---|---| | [`HomeView.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/HomeView.java) | The home screen | | [`HomeMode.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/HomeMode.java) | Switching between Free My TV and Original | | [`Adb.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/Adb.java) | The TV's own ADB, from inside the TV | | [`Recs.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/Recs.java) | The picks (TMDB) | | [`HomeData.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/HomeData.java) | Weather and prices | | [`HomeApps.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/HomeApps.java) | The shelf, inputs and All Apps | | [`DreamView.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/DreamView.java) | The screensaver | | [`SettingsActivity.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/SettingsActivity.java) | The settings screen (the app's icon) | | [`Prefs.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/Prefs.java) | Settings changed on the TV | | [`RemoteKeys.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/RemoteKeys.java) | The TCL remote's app buttons | | [`Watchdog.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/Watchdog.java) | The safety net | | [`web/home.js`](web/home.js) | The home screen on LG TVs | | [`web/tv.js`](web/tv.js) | The TV's apps and inputs, on LG and Samsung | | [`webos/build.py`](webos/build.py), [`webos/install.py`](webos/install.py) | The LG app package and its install | | [`tizen/build.py`](tizen/build.py) | The Samsung app package | The website ([freemytv.io](https://freemytv.io)) is in [`docs/`](docs): plain HTML, CSS and JS on GitHub Pages. ## Privacy No accounts, no analytics, no tracking. The app talks to TMDB, Open-Meteo (with the coordinates you set, or your time zone's main city), and Binance only when `show_crypto=true`. Your settings stay on your computer and your TV. ## Credits - Built with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code). - The LG version builds on what [@danielthejoker18](https://github.com/danielthejoker18) found in [FreeMyTvWebOS](https://github.com/danielthejoker18/FreeMyTvWebOS) (MIT): installing through Developer Mode and opening apps through the TV's service bus. - On Samsung TVs it installs with [TizenBrew Installer](https://github.com/reisxd/TizenBrewInstaller) by [@reisxd](https://github.com/reisxd). - This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by [TMDB](https://www.themoviedb.org/). - Weather data by [Open-Meteo.com](https://open-meteo.com/) (CC BY 4.0). Prices from the [Binance](https://www.binance.com/) public API. - Icons: [Material Symbols](https://fonts.google.com/icons) (Apache 2.0). Font: [Inter](https://rsms.me/inter/) (SIL OFL 1.1). Coin logos: [cryptocurrency-icons](https://github.com/spothq/cryptocurrency-icons) (CC0). - Not affiliated with Google, TCL, LG, Samsung or any streaming service. 简体中文 · English

(Surfaces 0-3, Clay, Hairlines, System Fonts)"] OCUI --> Atoms["2. 基础原子交互控件
(CdsButton, SegmentedControl, StatusIndicators, Dialog)"] OCUI --> Stream["3. 会话流与指令引擎

**交互式组件故事书 (Storybook Preview)**：内置单文件开箱即用的离线 Storybook，支持浏览器直接打开预览全部组件动效。 4. **七大领域分卷完整技术手册**：附带深度逆向分析开发手册 [`docs/Claude Design System (CDS).md`](docs/Claude%20Design%20System%20(CDS).md)。 --- ## 📚 七大篇章逆向分析手册 (Complete Technical Manual) 整个仓库最具工业价值的核心是这本长达 3,000+ 行、31 个核心子节的深度逆向工程手册：[`docs/Claude Design System (CDS).md`](docs/Claude%20Design%20System%20(CDS).md)。 它不仅记录了所有反编译源码取证位置，还详尽解构了 Anthropic 解决当代大模型产品前端痛点的系统架构方案： ### 📖 第一篇：设计哲学与设计令牌体系 * **[1.1 设计哲学与视觉调性](docs/01-设计哲学与设计令牌体系.md#11-设计哲学与视觉调性)**：温润的人文质感（Editorial Warmth）、四层低对比表面微阶梯、高帧率轻负担动效。 * **[1.2 级尺寸阶梯（XS/SM/MD/LG）、5 大变体（Primary/Secondary/Ghost/Outline/Danger）、`active:scale-[0.98]` 物理触觉。 * **[2.2 分段滑动选择胶囊](docs/02-基础原子组件与交互控件.md#22-分段滑动选择胶囊)**：999px 全圆角轨道、2px 几何内边距、纯几何绝对定位与 Framer Motion 事件防吞噬护盾、4px 移动死区、双击 50/50 吸附、边缘折叠门限与约束钳制。 * **[5.4 工件预览沙箱与隔离通信架构](docs/05-视听多媒体与产物交互物理学.md#54-工件预览沙箱与隔离通信架构)**：Epitaxy 隔离容器、7 大专有 MIME 分发、用户手势门禁与虚拟包重定向。 * **[5.5 桌面宿主深度融合与窗口材质](docs/06-系统级桌面架构与协作拓扑.md#61-macos-桌面宿主深度融合与窗口材质)**：`hiddenInset` 标题栏、交通灯逆缩放几何补偿、`-webkit-app-region: drag` 安全区、macOS Vibrancy 毛玻璃。 * **[6.2 items.description: One 8 KB skill that replaces REA (Reverse Engineer Anything): plain CLI tools, no MCP. Benchmarked: 38% faster, 35% cheaper.
items.readme:
# leanrea

**One 8 KB skill file that does what [REA](https://github.com/morluto/rea) does: no MCP server, no 207 tools, no setup.**

REA (Reverse Engineer Anything) puts an MCP layer between your agent and tools it can already use: asar, otool, nm, `go version -m`, jadx, apktool, Ghidra, tshark, binwalk, sqlite3. leanrea drops that layer. It tells the agent which command is fastest for each kind of target, gives it ready-to-paste recon commands, and lists the traps that REA's code handles for you. The agent then runs the real tools itself.

|  | REA 6.5.0 | leanrea |
|---|---|---|
| What gets installed | 25 MB npm package + MCP server | one `SKILL.md` |
| Instructions | 23.5 KB skill + 48.8 KB references | 8 KB |
| Tools added to the agent | 207 (3.35 MB of definitions) | 0 (uses Bash) |
| Context for "Reply OK", all tools loaded | 400.7k tokens, $1.60 | 34.5k tokens, $0.09 |

## Benchmark

Claude Code headless (`claude -p`), Sonnet 5.5, macOS arm64. 4 reverse-engineering tasks × 3 reps × 3 arms, with the arms run side by side. Answers are graded against hand-made keys.

| arm | total wall time | cost | turns | tokens | score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **leanrea** | **388 s** | **$2.17** | **55** | **2.40 M** | 74/75 |
| no skill | 479 s | $2.21 | 81 | 3.11 M | 67/75 (one refusal) |
| REA (MCP + its skill) | 627 s | $3.36 | 124 | 5.93 M | 75/75 |

Against REA, leanrea had **38% less wall time, 35% lower cost, 56% fewer turns and 60% fewer tokens, at the same accuracy**. Its one partial miss named an older IPC channel instead of the v2 one (both channels exist).

The tasks:
- **electron**: trace a feature through a real Electron app's app.asar (native function → main-process class → IPC channels).
- **native**: inventory the exports, a TCC permission check and the single-instance lock of that app's native addon (`.node`).
- **go**: toolchain and dependency versions of a stripped `gh` binary.
- **deep**: from disassembly alone, the exact socket path format, wire protocol and peer authentication of that lock.

The same operation run through REA's CLI vs the raw command:

| operation | REA | raw |
|---|---|---|
| Go build info | 0.56 s | `go version -m`: 0.06 s |
| Mach-O overview | 3.32 s | otool + dyld_info + nm: 0.04 s |
| Electron app analysis (real desktop app) | fails on asar integrity until you pass a flag, then **47.9 s and 140 MB of JSON** | asar extract + `rg -uu`: 4.8 s, 24 KB |

Full tables, the context-overhead runs and caveats: [bench/BENCHMARK.md](bench/BENCHMARK.md). Raw per-run metrics: [bench/results/final.jsonl](bench/results/final.jsonl).

**Caveats:**
- Only 3 reps per cell, one model, one machine.
- REA was tested in its best case: Claude Code's deferred tool search loads MCP tools on demand. Agents that load every tool pay the 400k-token row.
- Ghidra, Hopper and jadx weren't installed, so the native tasks ran on Xcode tools for both arms.
- The plain model is already good at this. leanrea's gain over no skill (about 19% faster, 32% fewer turns) is smaller than its gain over REA.

## Install

```sh
npx skills add aicodeking/leanrea
```

This uses the [skills CLI](https://skills.sh). It finds the `leanrea` skill and asks which agents to install it for: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and the others it supports.

Common variants:
```sh
npx skills add aicodeking/leanrea -g                    # install for your user, in every project
npx skills add aicodeking/leanrea -a claude-code -y     # Claude Code only, no prompts
npx skills add aicodeking/leanrea -g -a '*' -y          # every supported agent, user level
npx skills update leanrea                               # pull the latest version later
```

Manual install, if you prefer:
```sh
git clone https://github.com/aicodeking/leanrea
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cp -R leanrea/leanrea ~/.claude/skills/
```
If an agent has no skills support, paste `leanrea/SKILL.md` into its rules or system prompt; it is plain text.

Use it:
```
/leanrea How does the search feature in Foo.app work? Show the evidence.
```

## What's in the skill

- **Rules:**
  - Work on a copy.
  - Route by `file` and magic bytes first.
  - Slice minified files instead of reading them.
  - Batch probes into one shell call.
  - Search extracted trees with `rg -uu`, because bundlers hide code in dot-folders like `.webpack/`.
  - Mark each claim as seen, inferred or unknown.
- **Router:** the fastest command for each target type:
  - Electron/asar (IPC, preload, `contextBridge`, fuses)
  - minified web bundles and source maps
  - Hermes/bytenode
  - Mach-O (exports, imports, entitlements, ObjC/Swift)
  - native disassembly, ELF/PE
  - Go buildinfo, Rust cargo-auditable, .NET, Android APKs, the Flutter snapshot hash
  - WASM, SQLite, plists, pcap/HAR, firmware
  - websites and runtime tracing
- **First moves:** one paste-and-run command each for native binaries and Electron apps. Each gets the whole inventory in a single tool call.
- **Speed patterns:** start from strings and imports, find a string's function through the otool literal-pool comments, read call sequences rather than every instruction, and diff inventories before diffing code.

## Reproduce the benchmark

Needs macOS with the target Electron app installed (see `bench/setup.sh`), `gh` from Homebrew, Node, and Claude Code logged in.
```sh
cd bench
./setup.sh        # installs rea-agents@6.5.0, copies the targets into bench/work (gitignored)
./run_all.sh      # 36 runs, about $8 on Sonnet
./ctx.sh          # context-overhead probe
python3 mcp_list.py node work/rea-install/node_modules/rea-agents/scripts/rea.mjs --mcp   # REA tool count + size
```
The answer keys in `tasks.json` match the app versions used here and a `gh` built with go1.27.1. Other versions need new keys.

## Credit

REA is an impressive, well-documented project by the morluto team. Most of the gotchas in this skill came from reading their code and docs. leanrea isn't affiliated with REA. It is just a test of whether a model with plain tools and a short note can do the same work faster.

MIT licensed.
